main_text.p: In hac verò re idem summus philosophus dicit, melius habuisse hunc magistratum Carthaginensem, quàm ephoros Laconicos, quòd hi è cujusvis sortis hominibus, centum-viri autem ex optimis quibusque (ἐφόρες[?] μὲν ἐκ τῶν τυχόντων, τὰς δὲ τὰς ἑκατὸν ἀριστίνδην) electi fuerint: quod ipsum fanè ad aristocraticam rationem quoque propius accedit. Nec multò post subjicit ibidem hanc sententiam: μεγάλων γὰρ κύριοι πλουτοῦντες[?], ἂν δ' ἀτελεῖς[?] ὦσι, μεγάλα βλάπτειν, ἐλαχίστων[?] ἤδη τὴν πόλιν τῶν Λακεδαιμονίων: homines tenues ad magnam potestatem provecti multum nocent, & jam nocuère civitati Laceda-monioru̅m. Atque hos Centum-viros judices illos fuisse, in quorum tribunalibus Suffetes tempore Annibalis prætorum more actionem dirigentes sederint, de quibus Livius decad. iiii libro iiii scripsit, verisimillimum existimo. Morum quoque præfectos Carthaginem habuisse, cum res ejus florerent, Æmilius Probus nos docet. Sic enim scribit in vita Amilcaris. Erat cum Amilcare adolescens illustris & formosus Asdrubal, quem nonnulli diligi turpius quàm par erat, ab eo loquebantur: nec enim maledici tanto viro deesse poterant.

page.notes: Uncertain readings: the Greek words marked [?] (the first word of the first Greek passage, and several words of the second, which is set in italic) and the form "Laceda-monioru̅m" (the printed text reads "Laced-aemoniorum" with a line-end hyphen; the transcription keeps the printed spelling as far as it can be read). The paragraph does not visibly begin with an indent, so it is treated as a continuation; "In hac vero" may continue from page 13, but no cont="true" is set because this cannot be confirmed. The two small marks "o" and "8" below the last line at the far left are unclear: they may be a stray mark, a note reference or a signature, and are not transcribed. The scan has red edge marks and show-through at the margins, not transcribed.
